exposure: hospital certification status (certified vs. non-certified colorectal cancer centers)
time period (before vs. after certification within the same institutions)
outcome: utilization of preoperative imaging (endorectal ultrasound, pelvic MRI)
surgical quality indicators (M.E.R.C.U.R.Y. classification, anastomotic leakage rates)
cohort: The study included 14,905 patients with primary rectal cancer (UICC Stages I-III) treated at 271 hospitals.
finding: Hospital certification was associated with improved adherence to diagnostic protocols and reduced intraoperative complications, but it did not significantly impact surgical quality or long-term survival outcomes.
